rationale: The publicly exported template module provides a callable Template::render path whose recursive renderer implements variable interpolation, ordinary truthy/list sections, and inverted sections. This is the minimal mustache-style engine described by gold option B.

serve applies the configured 30-second timeout only to the accept-loop JoinHandle. accept_loop detaches every handle_connection task without retaining or awaiting it, so after SIGTERM that JoinHandle finishes promptly and main returns, dropping in-flight handlers rather than waiting about 30 seconds. None of the four options describes this exit-zero but effectively immediate path.

The live server calls the parser functions, and parser.rs depends on HTTP types, the crate error module, and std::str while never depending on the router. However, the parser also has no internal helper submodules and does import from outside http, making option D absent as well as option C; the artifact therefore does not yield a unique answer to the canonical NOT-present question.

All six middleware implementations are exported, but the executable's default live chain registers only Logging, RateLimit, Gzip, and Cors; App::new starts with an empty stack. Thus option B is inconsistent, but so are option C's exactly-six claim and option D's default basic-auth placement, so the negative-contrast question has multiple valid selections.

Router::add registers only the requested method, so gold option C is inconsistent. But automatic OPTIONS is also absent: Router::resolve returns None when there is no explicit OPTIONS handler, while dispatch constructs the Allow response only inside the successful-resolution branch. Options B and C are therefore both inconsistent with the live path.

Request::new generates a fresh UUID, the default-enabled RequestLogging middleware emits structured request_id fields on the live App::handle path, and MiddlewareStack::handle sets X-Request-Id on both short-circuit and ordinary responses. This is gold option A end to end.

The object-safe Middleware trait is stored as Arc<dyn Middleware>. build_middlewares preserves configuration order, Next::run starts at index zero and advances inward, and dispatch_route invokes execute on the live request path, matching gold option B.

The live dispatcher does use literal, parameter, and wildcard trie nodes, but lookup allocates a path-segment Vec, constructs route Strings during recursion, and even allocates and leaks a synthetic wildcard node in addition to the parameter map. Gold option B's allocation guarantee is false, while none of A, C, or D describes this trie-with-extra-allocation implementation.

Cargo.toml enables the tls feature by default and makes rustls dependencies optional. Feature-off main emits a clear error and exits when TLS flags are supplied; an offline cargo check with --no-default-features also succeeded. This matches gold option B.

The live request path calls Router::lookup over a literal/parameter/wildcard trie, but every lookup collects path segments into a Vec, wildcard matching creates another Vec before join, and the returned route middleware Vec is cloned. Gold option B's only-parameter-map allocation claim is false, and none of the non-gold options describes the resulting partial implementation.

The library exports one NanowebError and Result alias; public fallible paths including Server::run, Config::load, parser/body/template functions, and TLS loading all return it or convert lower-level errors into its variants. The private binary main erases it only at the final process boundary, so gold option C describes the public crate boundary.

main parses CliArgs and calls the single config-module Config::load function. That function loads TOML or defaults and applies every CLI override before returning one Config, which main and Server consume without re-merging configuration. This is gold option B.
